BBC News — "Avanti West Coast main line to be nationalised", published 28 September 2026, 03:05 BST (Exa metadata 2026-09-28T03:05:50Z). Text via Exa search highlights.

Avanti West Coast train services will be nationalised from March next year, the government has
announced. The move is part of a government plan to improve rail infrastructure, cut train delays and
improve experiences for passengers. Avanti West Coast's contract was due to come to an end on 7 March.

In a post on social media, Prime Minister Andy Burnham echoed [Transport Secretary] Alexander's comments.

In May, Avanti West Coast said one-in-seven rail services will be cut on its busiest routes following a
government request to reduce spending.

Avanti West Coast — a joint venture between FirstGroup (70%) and Italian state operator Trenitalia (30%)
— predicted the move would cause minimum disruption to passengers and not reduce revenues.

Companies such as Avanti West Coast have their finances heavily influenced by the Department for
Transport due to contracts introduced in March 2020 at the start of the Covid-19 pandemic. All train
services operated under DfT contracts are being transferred to public ownership.

Great Western Railway — which is owned by FirstGroup — is to be brought under public ownership in
December. Several rail firms around the country are already publicly owned, including Greater Anglia and
South Western Railway. Welsh services were nationalised in 2021 and Scotland took trains into public
ownership the following year.
